messages:
alex: Quick check — I spun up an initial bring-up for saucebite-6.7b (fp16/int8/int4). Smoke tests done + small eval set (summ-train-100 + micro-instr). Early signal: int4 shows ~12% drop on longform summarization (rougeL) but saves ~2.6x token cost. Posting raw numbers and a few notes. Need quick product/GTN guidance on routing vs holdback.

madhan: Can you drop the unit econ + latency numbers?

alex: Sure — quick summary:
```
cost_per_1k_tokens: fp16 $0.012  int8 $0.0075  int4 $0.0045
p50_latency (1 request, 512 tokens): fp16 120ms  int8 105ms  int4 95ms
throughput (seq len 512): fp16 250 toks/s  int8 380 toks/s  int4 620 toks/s
```
Notes: int4 inference runner uses hybrid KV packing, batch=8 for the tests. Env: dedicated devpool (A100s), same prompt set across runs.

clem: Quick quality snapshot (summ-train-100 longform):
- rouge1 / rougeL / bertscore (approx):
  - fp16: 44.1 / 38.5 / 0.86
  - int8: 43.6 / 37.9 / 0.855
  - int4: 38.9 / 33.8 / 0.82
Instruction-following micro (alpaca-like): exact-match %
  - fp16 71.2, int8 70.8, int4 68.1
So int8 is very close to fp16; int4 erosion is concentrated on long-context coherence and rare-token fidelity.

sara: From product/GTN perspective: longform summarization is a priority for some customers. A 12% relative drop on rougeL is material. Would prefer a hybrid routing approach rather than a full rollout. Also want a canary with quality alerts.

alex: Agree. PoC routing snippet I tested:
```
{
  "routes": [
    {"max_tokens": 512, "model": "saucebite-int4"},
    {"max_tokens": 1024, "model": "saucebite-int8"},
    {"model": "saucebite-fp16"}
  ],
  "fallback": "saucebite-fp16"
}
```
I'll wire this into the router flag and add a 5% canary before bumping.

eval-bot: eval summary uploaded: https://internal.eval.svc/saucebite/4632101234 — includes per-slice diffs + prompt-sensitivity heatmap :eyes:

clem: One more datapoint — priming length matters. When we prepend a long instruction template (~300 tokens) the int4 gap increases by ~3 pts rougeL. Shorter priming reduces the gap to ~6 pts. This suggests token-level quant noise accumulates with longer prefixes. Potential remediations: quant-aware soft prompts, selective higher-precision K/V for earlier layers, or hybrid KVC cache precision.

madhan: Unit-econ recommendation for GTN:
- Default: saucebite-int8 (1.6x cost savings vs fp16, <1 pt avg rougeL impact)
- Longform/enterprise: route to fp16 (preserve quality)
- Experimental/low-cost tier: expose saucebite-int4 behind a feature flag with explicit QA opt-in and per-route alerts
We should also set a per-route quality SLA: alert if rougeL drops >1.5 pts vs baseline on rolling 1k samples.

alex: Plan: canary int8 @10% next Tuesday, enable routing by token-length, add per-route eval hooks + alerting. I'll open a short report with detailed slice tables and config. Thanks all :heart:
